items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: But way before 52nd Street these things because -- and Monroe's Uptown House -- they used to -- that was all they did up there was jam all the time.

ctx.x: Yeah, and we'd jam all night over there, yeah. Things -- these things went on up to the -- about the early '40's. That's when they start slacking off. Well, the union started tightening up on it because a lot of guys, they wouldn't even hire any musicians and yet they could get all that music for nothing. And they were doing fantastic business. So, the union moved in. And, of course, I don't know. One thing Led to another.

Up at Minton's -- used to go at Minton's. Same thing. But even before modern jazz got up at Minton's, they used to run the sessions up there. A lot of guys used to go. I used to go up there and play a lot. But all over. They had these things on 52nd Street, all around. But way before 52nd Street these things because -- and Monroe's Uptown House -- they used to -- that was all they did up there was jam all the time.

I've heard that some of the major horn players used to carry their own rhythm sections with them for sessions. They'd go out after work and challenge somebody, but they'd bring along their own rhythm.
